whatChanged: quality.spec.mjs probes canPlayType for the fixture codec: a capable engine keeps the existing strict dimensions/seek assertions; an engine without H.264 must show the visible Playback Error overlay with a nonempty message and a working Go Back.

HLS-CORS accepts either a failed request or a failed response for the same denied manifest path, and accepts either the switching-engine warning or a classified mediaErrorCode 2, while retaining redaction and no-secret-log assertions.

source-preference.spec.mjs derives the expected preferred order from the engine's own H.264 capability and, when unsupported, still requires the 4K source to be selectable and to surface an explicit error with a return path.
notRelaxed: Chromium and Chrome report H.264 support, so the strict decode/seek/dimension branch still runs there and all 42 cases pass.
All eight sources remain present, toggle restores provider order, no extra media/provider request is made, provider-order autoplay is unchanged, and the no-secret-log assertion remains.
Unsupported-codec browsers must show an explicit user-visible failure, which is the product requirement rather than a skipped assertion.
limits: Playwright Firefox is a real Gecko engine but not branded-Firefox certification, and it runs an emulated x86_64 build on this ARM64 host.
Chrome for Testing is a real Chrome binary but not a user-profile installation.
No Microsoft Edge (no ARM64 Linux build or physical x64 device), Safari, iOS or physical mobile.
